_doc: Measured centrifugal-compressor rig cases used to calibrate and validate the surge/stall model. Geometry from the original reports where available; map points digitised from the cited figures (read-off uncertainty ~1 % in flow, ~0.5 % in PR).

hecc.source: NASA/CR-2014-218114/REV1 (Medic et al., 'High Efficiency Centrifugal Compressor for Rotorcraft Applications'); Appendix C blade/vane coordinates; vendored in boomsonic_v0 scripts/phase0_tools/vendor/data/hecc

geometry.note: vane_throat = throat_area 5.983e-3 / (20 x b3); 20 splitter vanes not blocking the throat; b3 pinched from 15.47 to 14.2 mm

surge.note: PR still rising at the last stable point (slope -0.41)

choke.note: vertical part of the measured 100 % line

cc3_vaned.source: Kulkarni, Beach, Skoch, 'Computational Study of the CC3 Impeller and Vaneless Diffuser Experiment' (NTRS 20140009577) Table 1 and Fig. 2; McKain & Holbrook NASA CR-204134 (1997) for the design; diffuser radii from Skoch's CC3 papers (approximate)

geometry.note: vane LE angle and throat not tabulated in the sources used: set by the suite's design rule (LE at the L2 vaneless-exit angle minus the design incidence; throat at M 0.70), which is flagged as an assumption

design.note: PR_ts 3.93 at 10.0 lbm/s from Fig. 2 (design-speed data, inlet ~86 kPa, corrected)

surge.note: leftmost measured point of the design-speed vaned line, 9.40 lbm/s; the paper does not state whether it is the surge point

cc3_vaneless.source: Kulkarni, Beach, Skoch (NTRS 20140009577) Fig. 8, design speed, vaneless diffuser (exit rating station R/R_TE 1.18)
cc3_vaneless.geometry_ref: cc3_vaned impeller with n_vanes 0, r4 = 1.18 r2

stable_range.note: lowest measured point 7.2 lbm/s with PR still rising (4.43): no stall down to at least 72 % of design flow
